summary: Typosquat of axios injects unrelated transitive dependencies
details: Package published as `@qwedqwed/axios` republishes the legitimate axios source (bundle matches axios 1.16.1 while package.json claims 1.16.3) under an unaffiliated npm scope. The `dependencies` block in package.json adds two packages that genuine axios does not declare and that no shipped code references: `@caspianph/storyteller` (an unaffiliated scope with no public reputation) and `math` (a long-standing squat target on the npm registry). Their only effect on a consumer is to be pulled into the install tree whenever `@qwedqwed/axios` is installed, at which point their own lifecycle scripts and module top-level code execute on the installer's machine. The bundled `dist/node/axios.cjs` is the unmodified axios source — `exec(` occurrences are `RegExp.prototype.exec` calls (DATA_URL_PATTERN, tokensRE, parseProtocol), not `child_process.exec`, and there is no shell-out, remote fetch, or obfuscation in the bundle itself. The supply-chain risk is the dependency injection via the typosquat name, not the axios bundle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
